segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
they were removing their sons and their daughters (or: their [fem.] sons and their [fem.] daughters?),
and sending them to distant regions.
Yet to be saved from his hands they were unable;
nor from the shameful act that he committed with them were they rescued (or: were they [fem.] rescued?).
And when for about four years, more or less, he had conducted himself in such disgraceful conduct,
and was wallowing in the mud of such wanton lust,
and was indulging in useless bodily pleasures,
he was greatly hated by all the governors of the provinces of his kingdom.
And in the year 1605 [of the Greeks, 1294 AD],
in the month of Tammuz, there came to him one of his cousins, who was called Baidu,
who also had a handsome son.
And while they were sitting at a drinking party of wine, eating and drinking and rejoicing,
as if in boldness {or: outspokenness}, Gaikhatu insulted Baidu.
Baidu, however, insulted him in return,
and accused him as if he were the son of a harlot.
Gaikhatu immediately became inflamed with rage,
and shouted out to those around him
that they should drag him outside the camp,
and beat him to death.
This was something that had never entered Baidu's mind,
nor had he expected from Gaikhatu such an act,
even though he had offended greatly.
And when they seized him,
and laid hands on him,
and stripped him outside the measure {or: bounds},
and dragged him and carried him off and put him in a small tent,
they were planning to kill him.
And when he had slept for an hour,
Gaikhatu sent the nobles who were around him to go and rebuke Baidu for the insolence (or: undisciplined behavior?) which had proceeded from him,
and for how he had belched out an insult against the King of Kings.
He, however, cunningly, as if in jest, mocked even these, saying: "Where is Gaikhatu? Bring wine so that we may drink!
What on earth happened? And how did I come to this small tent?" And with such talk he bewildered the hearers,
and persuaded many to believe as true that which was not true.
And Gaikhatu himself was easily persuaded and deceived,
and he regretted greatly the blows that he had inflicted upon Baidu.
And by all means he was striving to soothe him... {OCR?: Taraghai son of Hulagu?}
